coverage_audit.notes: Input was received as rendered page images together with the embedded PDF text layer, hence input_mode=MIXED. The chapter contains no true tables; all dimensional data is carried in figures, so tables_checked reflects that no table content was found rather than that tables were present and read. Figure content was read from captions, numbered notes and the embedded text of dimension labels. No value was read off drawing scale and no illegible digit was reconstructed by inference. Four specific figure items could not be read with confidence and are recorded as REFERENCE_ONLY with needs_verification rather than excluded: the perimeter dimension lines of Figure 5-7, the sliding-door panel sub-ranges of Figure 5-11, the printed metric area of closet c1 in Figure 5-12, and the imperial-only dimensions of Figure 5-19d. Item counting method: relevant_source_items_mapped_to_records equals the count of evidence objects across all records, since each evidence object localises one distinct source item; the same source item cited by two records is counted once per record and this is a known over-count of at most a few items.

records.concept: Bedroom ambient lighting: a single overhead ceiling-mounted fixture pouring light downward is no longer considered standard, and in most cases pleasant ambient lighting is supplied by sources other than a downlight. top_findings.why_useful: Bed-side clearance for bed making is the single most reusable hard geometry in the chapter, and the source cleanly separates the functional minimum from the comfortable target.
Area-to-capability threshold: it converts a room area directly into how many walls can carry furniture, which is exactly the decision a layout solver makes first.
Storage front clearance is object-state dependent (drawer open vs closed), a distinction that a naive footprint model would lose entirely.
Closet-to-entrance adjacency with an explicit frequency rationale, and it implies a traffic path from entry to closet that does not pass the bed.
One of the very few quantified efficiency relationships in the chapter: double loading yields 27 percent more rod per square foot of closet area.
